This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 13.08.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. petitioner being a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 41-EB-7647 which was ridden by his friend was proceeding near Matha Party Hall, Magadi Huliyurdurga Road, Someshwara Colony, Magadi,
Ramanagara, at that time, a Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NJ-1877 came from back side and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained SCCH-5 grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Government Hospital,
Magadi, thereafter shifted to Boss Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, for which he has spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 24 years, hale and healthy, working as Process Consultant, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., due to this accident, he has lost future income,
future prospective life, happiness and earning capacity.

Out of this accident crime No.247/2022 is registered against the driver of the said Bolero Car before the Magadi Police Station for the offences Rakesh Kumar vs Suguna Sundaram on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171967390/
2 punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said car, they are SCCH-5 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further submitted that, she is owner of the Bolero LMV Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-03- NJ-1877 and the said vehicle is insured with respondent No.2 vide its policy No.2011500201-20800589600000 valid since 10.02.2021 to 09.02.2024 and his son who has driven the car on the alleged date of accident was holding valid and driving license bearing No.KA05- 20130017454 valid till 20.08.2033.
Further submitted that, said Bolero vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident and denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, SCCH-5 hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and seeks protection under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, driver of the Bolero was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.

Further admitted issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bolero bearing Reg.No.
KA-03-NJ-1877 and denies the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the said vehicle in the alleged accident.
Further submitted that, petitioner was not wearing ISI mark headgear at the time of accident.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH-5 6.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 13.08.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NJ-1877?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW-2, examined Medical Record Technician at Boss Multispeciality Hospital as PW-3, Duty Doctor at Magadi Government Hospital by name SCCH-5 Dr.Pallavi K.L. is examined as PW-4 and marked 23 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.23 and closed his evidence.

On Rakesh Kumar vs Suguna Sundaram on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171967390/
3 the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts SCCH-5 averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of statement is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.5,
copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of reply is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.8 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.10.
10 . Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined Doctors as PW-2 and PW-4, Medical Record Technician as PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-4 and records those have marked i.e., as FIR, complaint, statement, spot mahazar, sketch, Sec.133 notice, reply, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident SCCH-5 dated 13.08.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 13.08.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. while he was proceeding as pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EB-7647 near Matha Party Hall, Magadi Huliyurdurga Road, Someshwara Colony, Magadi, Ramanagara.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
SCCH-5 12.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the Bolero car driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.

Accordingly I have answered above Issue Rakesh Kumar vs Suguna Sundaram on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171967390/
4 No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained bimalleolus fracture left ankle, for which, he underwent surgery in the form of ORIF + TBW for fracture of medial malleolus,
CRIFwith tens for fracture lateral malleolus.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.9, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.11 issued by Boss Speciality Clinics & Diagnostic Centre, wherein he took SCCH-5 treatment as indoor patient since 14.08.2022 to 17.08.2022 and for the second time he took treatment as inpatient from 18.04.2023 to 19.04.2023.

Further he has furnished medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.14, medical bills amounting to Rs.91,692/- marked as Ex.P.15 and advance receipts are marked as Ex.P.16.
14.
Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital is examined as PW-2 .

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD Card marked as Ex.P.17 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.18 and he has assessed total disability of left lower limb at the rate of 36% and whole body disability at the rate of 18%.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and implants is removed on 18.04.2023.
Further deposed that, he has not conducted functional disability.
SCCH-5 15.

Further Medical Record Technician at Boss Multispeciality Hospital by name Mahesh Kumar is examined as PW-3 and he has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.19, case sheet marked as Ex.P.20 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.21.
In cross- examination deposed that, he does know about the treatment given to the petitioner.
16. Dr.Pallavi K.L. Duty Doctor at Magadi Government Hospital is examined as PW-4 and exhibited copy of Police Intimation marked as Ex.P.22 and copy of MLC Extract marked as Ex.P.23.
In cross-examination she has deposed that, she has given initial treatment to the petitioner and further she admitted that, she has written MLC Extract.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in SCCH-5 (2011)
1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 12% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 36% of left lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

17. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 24 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 05.01.1998 and the alleged accident is occurred on 13.08.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 his age is considered about 25 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

5 18. As per his case, he was working as Process Consultant at HGS Global Solutions Pvt. Ltd., thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.11, petitioner took treatment as inpatient twice at Boss Multispeciality Clincs & Diagnostic Centre from 14.08.2022 to 17.08.2022 an from 18.04.2023 to 19.04.2023 i.e., for 4 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.14,750/-
p.m.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,967/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
20. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.15 medical bills for Rs.91,692/- and advance receipts are marked as Ex.P.16.
On perusal of the said SCCH-5 bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.9 in which Doctor who have treated i.e., Dr.Pallavihas categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 13.08.2022.

So as per Ex.P.9 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained abrasion wound over right parietal region, abrasion wound both buttocks, tenderness and swelling on left ankle joint, tenderness on left hip, left knee and bimalleolar fracture of left ankle,
which is grievous injury.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Steven Kumar for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338, 304(A) of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW-4 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged SCCH-5 accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.91,692/-.
21.
Per contra, except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of him to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.

Ofcourse during the course of argument, Sri.RSS counsel for respondent No.2 argued that, there is one day delay in lodging the complaint and Rakesh S/o. Shivanji is not pertaining to petition and father name in MLC not tallied SCCH-5 and treated Doctor not examined, but said arguments of respondent No.2 have not Rakesh Kumar vs Suguna Sundaram on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171967390/
6 supports his case, because they are not much importance in present type of case.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.

22. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl
. No .
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 3,82,320-00 2.
Pain and
sufferings 15,000-00
3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 91,692-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 1,967-00 period Total 5,20,979-00 23.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,20,979/- with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy in respect of Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NJ-1877 in favour of respondent No.1 bearing No.201150020120800589600000 which is valid for the period from 10.02.2021 to 09.02.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 13.08.2022
it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2 /insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

SCCH-5 25. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,20,979/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Twenty Thousand Nine Hundred Seventy Nine Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Rakesh Kumar vs Suguna Sundaram on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171967390/
7
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
SCCH-5 The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
